reader_notes: Reads as an authentic Swedish insändare/debattartikel. The opening scene is concrete and physical (slocknat elljusspår mitt i ett intervallpass, spången över kärret, pannlampor och minne, en hand på grannens axel), the middle is administrative in the right register (fritidsnämnden, tjänsteskrivelse, driftsrapport), and the close is a normal insändaravslutning with a concrete yrkande. No calques, no machine-translation flatness; the idiom is native ('ungefär vad en enda grusleverans till spåret gick på i våras', 'kan spåret gott släckas tidigt', 'leta sig tillbaka till parkeringen').

Internal consistency holds where it matters. The shift ends kvart i åtta, gruppen samlas halv nio, and the lights now go at 21 — the complaint is coherent. The byline (processoperatör och kvällslöpare) matches 'Mitt skift på bruket' and the 'processoperatörer' listed in the group. Timeline holds too: beslut i september, gäller sedan 1 oktober, text written in November ahead of novembermötet.

Q1 is anchored by an explicit sentence — 'Kalkylen utgår ändå från de gamla lamporna' — and the arithmetic reconciles: 38 000 with förbrukningen down by roughly two thirds lands near 12 700, matching 'omkring tolv tusen kronor'. I committed C without hesitation.

Q1 option B is a well-built near-miss: the single August count IS criticised in the text, but as support for 'begränsat för flertalet motionärer', not as part of the besparingskalkyl. The stem's word 'besparingskalkyl' is what keeps the item clean; a hurried reader could land on B.

The friction I felt, and why I did not call this fully natural: the writer states 'I augusti är det ljust till halv tio' and then concedes that 'mellan maj och augusti kan spåret gott släckas tidigt, för då gör belysningen ingen nytta'. By his own premise the window 21:30–23:00 in August is dark, so the summer concession quietly undercuts his own dark-hours argument. Real opinion writers make exactly this rhetorical move, so it does not break the text — but a careful reader notices the seam.

Second, smaller gap: the concrete proposal covers maj–augusti (släck vid nio) and oktober–mars (håll tänt till elva), leaving April and September unspecified. Typical of a real insändare, but it is a loose edge.

Q2 was unambiguous — 'för sommaren har nämnden faktiskt en poäng' plus 'håll tänt till elva från oktober till mars' gives B directly. Distractor C ('fel verksamhet') is a sharp near-miss because the title primes 'fel ...', but the text never argues for saving elsewhere, only at other hours. The title 'Fel timmar att spara in på' does lean toward the key and helps a test-wise reader drop C and D early; that is a normal headline effect rather than a defect.

Plausibility of facts: swapping kvicksilverlampor for led as late as vintern 2023 is late relative to the EU phase-out, but Swedish municipalities have done exactly that on tight budgets, and a two-thirds drop in förbrukning is realistic. Nothing read as a wrong fact. The 'kartan i montern lyser för övrigt vidare' detail is the kind of concrete irony a real local writer finds.
